anomalies.observed: On both MCU sheets the VCAP pins (FCC1 pins 48 and 73; NAVC1 VCAP_1/VCAP_2) carry explicit no-connect (X) markers, while the 2.2 µF capacitors flagged with the VCAP-specific note 'C13, C14: ESR < 100mOhm' (and 'C37, C38: ESR < 100mOhm') are wired to the VREF+ net (VREF+_FCC / VREF+_NAVC) instead of to the VCAP pins.
anomalies.expected: STM32 VCAP pins must be decoupled to GND with low-ESR capacitors (the 'ESR < 100mOhm' note is ST's VCAP requirement); VREF+ needs only its own small decoupling (100 nF/1 µF, already provided by C29/C30 and C37/C38-equivalent). The low-ESR 2.2 µF parts belong on VCAP, not on VREF+.

evidence.quote: C13, C14: ESR < 100mOhm ... C13 2u2, C14 2u2 tied to VREF+_FCC; pins 48 'VCAP' and 73 'VCAP' marked X (no-connect) — Flight Control Computer (FCC) sheet
C37, C38: ESR < 100mOhm ... C37 2u2, C38 2u2 tied to VREF+_NAVC; VCAP_1/VCAP_2 pins marked X — Navigation Computer (NAVC) sheet
Where it is silent, judge the design with standard electrical-engineering practice and with the component's own metadata

anomalies.impact: The MCU internal core regulator is left with no output capacitor, so the H753 and F405 cannot power up / regulate correctly; the board would fail to boot (the VREF+ pin is also over-loaded with low-ESR bulk capacitance). This contradicts the specification's description of a working dual-MCU flight controller.

parsed.summary: The drawing otherwise matches the specification (correct MCU parts, sensor set, power stage, I2C addresses, and the documented barometer RESET/EOC swap), but both MCU sheets leave the VCAP pins no-connected while placing the low-ESR 2.2 µF VCAP capacitors on the VREF+ net, which would prevent the MCUs' core regulators from operating.
